subject.title: Discord compaction still fails with provider_error_4xx after #90496 closure on 2026.6.5

question: What should OpenClaw do when a Discord-bound Codex compaction fails with HTTP 403/provider_error_4xx and the channel remains over budget?
rationale: Source shows the current failure boundary, but choosing whether to rotate, preserve, fail with auth repair guidance, or avoid rebinding is user-visible session and provider policy rather than a source-only cleanup decision.

options.title: Define Discord recovery policy
options.body: Keep #92598 canonical and require live Discord/Codex proof before implementing session rotation, transcript preservation, or provider-specific recovery.

options.title: Fold into timeout work only with 403 proof
options.body: Treat #92899 as sufficient only if it adds explicit Discord provider_error_4xx evidence and covers the Codex HTTP 403 path.

options.title: Reclassify as auth support
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide HTTP 403 compaction failures are provider-auth repair guidance rather than an OpenClaw recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Define Discord recovery policy
recommendation.body: Keep #92598 canonical and require live Discord/Codex proof before implementing session rotation, transcript preservation, or provider-specific recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant owns the most recent merged partial fix and explicitly scoped out the remaining production provider_error_4xx and rotation policy decision.
